title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 115
paragraphs: While the boy thus spoke, a sense of recognition came over Astyages. The features of his face seemed to resemble his own, his answer appeared to be somewhat too free for his station, and the time of the exposure seemed to agree with the age of the boy. Struck with amazement by these things, he was for a while speechless. Having at length with difficulty recovered himself, he said, wishing to dismiss Artembares so that he might get the herdsman alone and examine him: “Artembares, I will so order these things that you and your son shall have no cause to find fault.” So he dismissed Artembares, and the servants, upon the command of Astyages, led Cyrus within. When the herdsman was left alone with the king, Astyages asked him where he had got the boy from and who had delivered him. The herdsman said that he was his own son, and that the boy's mother was living with him still as his wife. But Astyages said he was not well advised in wishing to be brought to extreme necessity, and as he said this he signaled to the spearmen of his guard to seize him. So as he was being led away to torture, the herdsman declared the story as it really was, and beginning from the beginning he went through the whole, telling the truth about it, and finally ended with entreaties, asking to be pardoned.
